correctness.rationale: The scalar published statistic reduces algebraically to scaled half-sample Student statistics. Under the Gaussian null, the two Student variables are independent, symmetric, and have signs independent of magnitudes, which gives the exact finite-sample law and cutoff. Under local alternatives, joint Student convergence, an orthogonal Gaussian rotation, and an explicit one-crossing conditional-rejection comparison prove strict asymptotic power dominance. The proof covers all stated m, alpha, and fixed nonzero h; numerical checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The claim resolves a concrete calibration and efficiency question for the canonical scalar Gaussian instance of a published cross-fitted statistic. The exact finite-sample null law converts an explicitly noted non-Gaussian calibration obstacle into a one-dimensional convolution quantile, while the single-crossing theorem proves that using both complementary directions strictly improves local power over the published single split for every nonzero local signal. This is a natural benchmark and boundary case for multiple-splitting methods, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
